newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up on Dadas, Primofin merger news.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up on Dadas, Primofin merger news.

text.p: Slovenian shares climbed 1.19 percent on Monday after financial consultancy Dadas announced it was weighing a merger with rival Primofin.
The SBI index rose 14.18 points to 1,206.5 in trade that was extended by 30 minutes due to technical problems.
Overall six shares rose, eight fell and two were unchanged while eight were untraded.

Shares in financial consultancy Primofin soared 74.64 percent on the merger news to 44,900 tolars on volume of 607 shares for total turnover of 26.7 million tolars. It was by far the day's biggest gainer.
Traders said Promofin had benefitted from expectations of a 1:4 share swap but others put the move down to speculative buying.
Neither Promofin nor Dadas would comment on the details of the proposed deal. A final decision will be taken at the shareholders' meetings of both companies on November 29.

In contrast, Dadas shares slumped 33.3 percent to 15,660 tolars on volume of 632 shares for total turnover of 102.1 million tolars. It was the biggest decliner and also the most actively traded stock.
"Serious investors are avoiding Dadas and shares connected to Dadas and will keep avoiding them in the future," another trader said.
Dadas shares have plunged 93 percent since late March when the securities market watchdog said it aimed to bar Dadas' mutual fund Proficia Dadas because of alleged trading irregularities.
Overall turnover fell to 229.4 million tolars from 525.5 million on Monday. --Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
